title: First recruitment: ONSS identification
summary: Before the first hiring, obtain employer status with ONSS via WIDE.
body: The company must have a BCE number and request employer identification. This obligation also applies to individuals, nonprofits, and administrations that hire their first worker.

After WIDE processing, ONSS communicates the definitive ONSS number, NACE code, and employer categories. Verify this data with the payroll manager: registration in the employer registry allows introduction of Dimona and DmfA. Reference: ONSS instructions 2026/3.

title: Dimona: declare entry and exit
summary: Declare entry at the latest when work actually begins and exit within the ONSS timeframe.
body: Dimona IN states the date the contractual relationship begins, even if the first work occurs later. It must be submitted no later than when the worker actually begins working.

Dimona OUT must arrive no later than the first working day following the end of the contractual relationship. An end date already entered exempts you from a new OUT if it remains accurate. A contract suspension or shift to part-time does not constitute an exit. ONSS instructions 2026/3.

title: Dimona: choose OTH, STU, FLX or EXT
summary: The Dimona type must match the actual employment regime and contribution scheme.
body: In ONSS instructions 2026/3, OTH covers workers without a specific type, notably students without solidarity contribution. STU targets student contracts subject to this contribution. FLX designates flexi-jobs.

EXT concerns occasional work in agriculture, horticulture, hospitality, funeral services, and corresponding temporary work. It may also apply to an occasional student without solidarity contribution. Do not choose EXT for every short contract: first check the conditions of the occasional work regime.

title: DmfA: quarterly declaration
summary: Prepare DmfA with employment and payroll data; Dimona does not replace it.
body: ONSS instructions 2026/3 set ordinary deadlines at April 30, July 31, October 31, and January 31, respectively for the first, second, third, and fourth quarters. The employer or their representative submits the declaration within the month following the quarter.

The data serves to calculate contributions and establish social rights. Keep receipts and correct errors within the prescription deadline. ONSS may still check and rectify a declaration already processed.

title: First hirings: reduction since July 2026
summary: Recalculate aid based on the date the right opens and rules effective July 1, 2026.
body: The budget law of May 30, 2026 reduces the first employee ceiling to EUR 2,000 per quarter, without time limit, including for ongoing reductions. For new rights as of July 1, 2026, the second to fifth employees each open a maximum reduction of EUR 1,000 over 12 quarters, to be chosen over 20 quarters. These ceilings correspond to full-time work.

Verify staff numbers for the preceding 12 months and the technical operating unit: a new legal entity is not sufficient. Prior rights follow the transitional provisions detailed by ONSS. Flexi-jobs, hospitality extras, and students under solidarity do not count toward this reduction. Have the rank and DmfA code validated before including the aid in your budget.

title: Flexi-jobs: open sectors and exclusions
summary: As of July 1, 2026, private and public sectors are open in principle; check activity and function exclusions.
body: ONSS instructions exclude domestic staff (CP 323, category 037); funeral services (CP 320), except occasional workers declared E; agriculture (CP 144); horticulture (CP 145), except parks and gardens; maritime fishing (CP 143), except shore personnel (category 019) and warehouse staff (category 086). Fish sales (category 186) remain excluded.

Artistic functions covered by the law of December 16, 2022 remain excluded, as do tasks falling under health care professions in the coordinated law of May 10, 2015 and occupations covered by the law of May 3, 2024 on sex work. A health facility thus cannot use a flexi-job for regulated care acts.

In voucher services, flexi-jobs are limited to the first three months after the first Dimona in the company; continuation thereafter requires a standard open-ended contract. The instruction of September 16, 2026 also confirms a 20% annual ceiling on employment volume for the Flemish childcare sector concerned: https://www.socialsecurity.be/employer/instructions/dmfa/fr/latest/intermediates.

title: Flexi-jobs: access and minimum wage
summary: Check prior employment or pension status and apply the minimum wage corresponding to the sector.
body: The worker must have worked at least 4/5 with other employers in T-3. Legal pensioners are exempt from this requirement. Moving from 100% in T-4 to 80% in T-3 excludes flexi-jobs in T and T+1. Also check ordinary employment with the employer, linked companies, and severance payments, according to ONSS exceptions.

As of September 1, 2026, the hospitality minimum hourly wage is EUR 12.11 plus EUR 0.93 holiday pay, totaling EUR 13.04. Elsewhere, respect the function schedule or, if absent, the RMMMG converted to hourly rate. Holiday pay is 7.67%; employer contribution is 28% on salary and holiday pay.

Conclude the written master contract and flexi contracts before work begins. In temporary work, the master provisions appear in the temporary work contract. Also check the applicable salary ceiling on the ONSS page.

The instruction of September 10, 2026 clarifies that in temporary work, ordinary work in T-3 with the same agency does not count toward the 4/5, even with another user: https://www.socialsecurity.be/employer/instructions/dmfa/fr/latest/intermediates.

title: Flexi-job: Dimona FLX and OK response
summary: A correct, timely, and accepted Dimona FLX is essential to the flexi regime.
body: Submit FLX before work and verify the OK response. Checks focus notably on T-3 career data and reduction in work volume. Late declaration does not allow declaring occupation as flexi in DmfA.

Declare separately each quarter, even if the contract continues. For an oral contract, establish a daily Dimona with actual start and end times, including when the shift crosses midnight. For a written contract, work must also be recorded according to ONSS procedures. Reference: 2026/3 instructions.

title: Hospitality extras: two-day limits and contingents
summary: A hospitality extra falls under occasional work for occupation of maximum two consecutive days.
body: The regime applies to fixed-term contracts or clearly defined work, directly in hospitality or via a temporary agency. Beyond two consecutive days with the same employer or user, all work must fall under the standard regime.

According to ONSS instructions 2026/3, flat-rate contributions are limited to 50 days per calendar year for the worker and 200 days for the employer. Both contingents must still contain days. These are limits of the favorable regime, not a prohibition on working more.

In the third quarter of 2026, the flat rate is EUR 11.52 per hour started, capped at EUR 69.12, or EUR 69.12 per day according to Dimona. These contribution bases are not minimum wages. Use the occasional work declaration and corresponding DmfA.

title: Students: 650-hour quota
summary: Check your Student at work balance before reserving hours with reduced contributions.
body: Since January 1, 2025, the federal annual quota is 650 hours. The reduced personal contribution is 2.71%, versus 13.07% under the standard regime. My Student at work and the app allow the student to track their balance.

Exceeding the quota remains possible, but additional hours fall under standard contributions. A student contract remains necessary if status conditions are met. After 12 months of continuous work with the same employer, a student contract is no longer possible with that employer. Tax rules and family allowances must be checked separately.

title: Students: reserve hours in Dimona STU
summary: Sign the student contract before Dimona STU and reserve hours by quarter.
body: The prior STU declaration must be based on a signed contract and state the planned hours for each quarter covered. Each hour started counts as one full hour. Do not declare a quarter without work or a zero-hour reservation.

Without prior STU, solidarity contribution is refused even if quota remains available. Adjust planned hours no later than the last day of the month following the quarter; after DmfA submission, a Dimona modification no longer adjusts the contingent. Reserve just enough to avoid unnecessarily blocking available hours. Reference: ONSS instructions 2026/3.

title: Foreign worker: single permit and exemptions
summary: Verify work and residence rights before setting the start date for a foreign candidate.
body: Since January 3, 2019, the single permit combines work and residence authorizations for the non-EU national working more than 90 days. The employer files through the single window; the Region examines the work and the Immigration Office the residence. Some cases, notably professional stays under 90 days and au pair arrangements, remain subject to other procedures.

Nationals of the EEA and Switzerland are exempt from work authorization, as also specified at https://www.belgium.be/fr/emploi/venir_travailler_en_belgique/permis_de_travail. For other candidates, examine the residence title and its labor market access: unlimited access may avoid a new authorization tied to the employer. Filing a request does not authorize work.

Prepare the residence documents requested by the Immigration Office: passport, proof of payment, resources, health insurance, medical certificate, and for adults, judicial record extract. Add professional documents required by the competent Region.

title: Posting: prior Limosa declaration
summary: The foreign employer must declare the work subject to Limosa before work begins in Belgium.
body: The prior declaration produces an L-1 receipt. The employer must transmit it for presentation to the Belgian user before the work; inspection services may also request it.

The system targets notably employees who work temporarily or part-time in Belgium while normally falling under foreign occupation. Check exemptions on the Limosa portal before concluding that a mission escapes declaration. Limosa is not work or residence authorization. Reference: ONSS instructions 2026/3.

title: Belgian client: check Limosa L-1 form
summary: Before work by a posted employee, request proof of Limosa and report its absence to ONSS.
body: The final user or Belgian ordering party checks the declaration before any direct or subcontracted work. It requests the L-1 receipt from the service provider or worker involved.

If the document cannot be presented, the client or their representative submits the "L-1 form absent" declaration via Limosa. Keep the receipt: this legal notice relieves the client of responsibility for this declaration obligation. Reference: ONSS instructions 2026/3.

title: Personnel register and Dimona exemption
summary: Determine whether a register remains required for hired persons and work locations.
body: Since January 1, 2003, the employer covered by Dimona benefits from the general register exemption for declared workers. They must nevertheless keep a register for workers outside Dimona scope. Also examine obligations and exemptions relating to the special register in case of multiple work locations.

When a register is required, number workers in the order they begin work. Enter identity data no later than when they start and the contract end date within seven calendar days thereafter. Arrange access to documents for inspections at the relevant locations.

title: Individual account: content and delivery to employee
summary: Open the individual account upon hiring and plan its delivery to the worker.
body: The account records work and compensation by pay period, with deductions and quarterly and annual totals. It must identify the employer and worker before use. Compensation elements are entered no later than when they become due. A pay statement remains due at each final settlement.

Deliver identification data within two months of the worker's start. The complete annual copy is due before March 1 of the following year; if departure occurs during the year, within two months of the end of the quarter of departure. The regulatory framework is the Royal Decree of August 8, 1980, published August 27, 1980; the practical page consulted bears no update date.

title: Construction sites: record attendance with Checkinatwork
summary: Plan daily recording before work on construction sites subject to Checkinatwork.
body: For construction work, the threshold is EUR 500,000 excluding VAT. Recording concerns people executing the work, including the self-employed; the company and executor must ensure it has been done. The system also covers certain meat sector activities in establishments subject to AFSCA.

Identify the site and agree beforehand on who records attendance before the start of each day's work. The notice published July 30, 2026 announces the shift of construction work to Check in and out at Work on April 1, 2027. As of September 30, 2026, this shift is not yet applicable.

title: Cleaning: record check-ins, check-outs and breaks
summary: Plan Check In and Out at Work for building cleaning activities involved.
body: Since September 1, 2024, the worker records on site the start and end of activity as well as breaks. The obligation also applies to self-employed, temporary workers, and interns executing activities within the system's scope.

The regime applies to cleaning real estate for a third party when the declaration falls under thresholds applicable to construction work. Check the scope of the construction declaration before configuring access. A simple daily attendance note does not replace the recording of check-outs and breaks.
